title: Merlin: Multi-View Representation Learning for Robust Multivariate Time Series Forecasting with Unfixed Missing Rates

problem.claim: Multivariate time series forecasting models are susceptible to missing values whose distribution changes over time, disrupting the semantics of the data.

gap.claim: Existing models lack robustness to missing values with changing distributions, resulting in suboptimal forecasting performance.

contributions.claim: Merlin is a multi-view representation learning approach that aligns incomplete observations with different missing rates to complete observations.
Merlin combines offline knowledge distillation with multi-view contrastive learning.
The contrastive-learning module constructs positive and negative pairs from incomplete observations with different missing rates to promote semantic alignment.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four real-world datasets demonstrate the reported superiority of Merlin.
The authors report that Merlin enhances robustness against unfixed missing rates while preserving forecasting accuracy.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multivariate time series forecasting predicts future values of multiple interrelated time series, and deep learning models mine global and local semantics from the data.
Missing values caused by malfunctioning data collectors disrupt time-series semantics, while their changing distribution creates robustness challenges for existing models.
Merlin aligns incomplete observations with different missing rates to complete observations through offline knowledge distillation and multi-view contrastive learning.
The authors report improved robustness to unfixed missing rates while preserving forecasting accuracy.
The authors report experiments on four real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: Missing-rate distributions can change over time and reduce the robustness of forecasting models.

interpretation.claim: Robust forecasting may require representations that remain aligned across incomplete observations with different missing rates.

application.claim: Use teacher-guided distillation and contrastive pairs across missing-rate conditions when adapting forecasting models to variable missingness.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how the approach performs outside the reported four real-world datasets or under missingness patterns not evaluated there.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the missing-value mechanisms, missing-rate ranges, or implementation details.
The abstract does not provide ablation results separating the contributions of the two modules.
